scope: One shared body reader for only course-progress POST and activity-results POST. No schema, session, authorization, live-identity, storage, SQL, quiz-scoring or client retry policy changes.

original.observations: The actual previous native JSON method accepted a pre-aborted valid request, ignored a mid-read abort until EOF, accepted an8192-byte padded valid payload, and stayed pending past an8250ms observation. Native malformed/transport errors were caught as null by both original routes.
original.limit: Local native Request/ReadableStream and actual pure validators only; this is not an externally executed attack or production availability measurement.

transportDecision.utf8: Nonfatal UTF8 and removal of one initial BOM match the previous native Request.json behavior. Split multibyte input and real cross-realm Uint8Arrays remain accepted.

schemaCapJustification.limit: These are actual existing schema maxima under compact canonical numbers and fullyUnicode-escaped string keys/values. Arbitrarily redundant whitespace, duplicate JSON keys or noncanonical arbitrarily long numeric representations are intentionally subject to the new wire cap; no claim that every semantically equivalent unbounded serialization still fits.

transportDecision.validationPolicy: Arbitrary JSON values still reach the original domain validators. Malformed JSON, missing/locked reader and arbitrary transport errors still become null, preserving each original domain-specific400 response. There is no unbounded req.json or req.text compatibility fallback.
transportDecision.sizePolicy: The new wire cap deliberately also limits redundant whitespace, duplicate-key encodings and arbitrarily verbose numeric forms. It does not claim every unbounded serialization of an otherwise valid value remains accepted.
transportDecision.errorPolicy: Only locally created branded transport errors are public:413 LEARNING_REQUEST_TOO_LARGE and408 LEARNING_REQUEST_ABORTED or LEARNING_REQUEST_TIMEOUT. Invocation-local ownership prevents errors from another read or status-shaped transport values from selecting a response.
transportDecision.abortBoundary: Before acquisition, before/after awaited read, EOF, parsing and return; each route immediately checks again after awaiting the reader and before its unchanged validator/database entry.
transportDecision.cleanup: Cancel only the acquired reader, at most once and without awaiting cleanup; clear timer, remove signal listener and attempt release. Stalled, rejected or throwing cleanup cannot replace a result.
transportDecision.notPromised: The8-second timer bounds body reading only. It is not a database/workflow deadline or rollback after server-side work has begun.

nativeCoverage: All232current course entries at valid maximal progress in canonical and fullyUnicode-escaped key/value JSON, with initial BOM.
Maximal structurally valid activity plus actual persistable Ansitz values; quiz remains forbidden.
Native JSON decoding parity, exact4096/4097wire boundaries, dishonest header, malformed lengths, split UTF8 and cross-realm bytes.
Pre/acquisition/pending/chunk/EOF/decoding/parse/post-await aborts; actual8000ms total deadline with a dribbling chunk at7200ms.
Owned cleanup, arbitrary transport/status errors, a prior reader interruption, original400 shapes and private no-store responses.
Actual synthetic signed unpaid owners, generation/deletion gates, revocation while body pending, owner-scoped writes, schema rejection and quiz ban.
Event retry, duplicate/conflicting IDs, lost acknowledgement, transient insert failure and two-owner composite identity.
validation.harnessAudit: The existing personal-data POST suite uses real NextRequest bodies. The private-statistics suite covers GET/isolated PostgreSQL generation rights. Other rg matches mostly inject course-progress-server into unrelated routes. No plain json callback was bypassed and no old test fixture needed modification.
validation.environment: Required tests use the sanitized allowlisted environment and NoNet preload. App secrets/live opt-ins are not inherited; database doubles and an existing ephemeral PGlite PostgreSQL fixture are isolated from customer systems.
